text.p: Unionized workers at Venezuela's national telephone company CANTV said Friday they were continuing their national strike after fruitless pay talks with the company Thursday night.
"The indefinite strike goes on," Cruz Hernandez, president of the Federation of Telecommunications Workers (Fetratel) told Reuters.
Representatives of Fetratel, which represents 29 unions and about one-third of CANTV's 17,000 workers, and CANTV met Thursday night to hammer out a deal in the pay dispute.
But, according to Hernandez, the talks were "fruitless because they (CANTV) presented the same scheme they always do."

CANTV workers are holding out for a 140 percent pay rise. Hernandez said CANTV's latest offer was a 20 percent rise backdated to January with a further 10 percent increase in July and another 15 percent in 1998.
Unionized workers started their strike Thursday morning, but CANTV said the walkout had not affected operations and that the vast majority of employees had ignored the strike call.
